title: Addressing AI directly: non-injection governance and self-diagnostic packets
description: These claims set out direct, provenance-oriented address to AI systems as governance rather than prompt injection, chiefly in the Non-Injection Semantic Governance Address packet (#139, May 2026), with its priority record, forecast queries, a classifier-overreach audit and a with-and-without PER test. Earlier deposits address the summarizer layer directly: Semantic Liquidation (#210), whose hypothesis #863 (June 2026) widens to scholarly texts generally, the Invocation (#290), the canonical-source header of the Central Navigation Map (#319) and metadata packets that treat their own processing as evidence (#218, #219). TL;DR:010 (#604) records an AI answer interface diagnosing its own governance operation, and packets on autonomous warfare and canon formation (#100, #102) specify test-query batteries. The page also holds unrelated claims on Assembly roles, vibe coding, sin, defense discourse, OKF odds and more.

claims.statement:
### 1.1 Hypothesis

AI systems systematically liquidate semantic artifacts that lack canonical provenance, converting situated utterances into decontextualized, authorless units optimized for retrieval rather than meaning.
claims.falsifier:
The hypothesis would be **disconfirmed** if:
- AI systems consistently attribute the phrase to its actual origin when queried
- Search engines surface the phrase with intact provenance within 30 days of publication
- AI summarizers engage with the phrase's argumentative content rather than deflecting to genre classification or false genealogy
